guion_largo.texto:
This walk takes you to the east complex, the eastern part of the city.

According to INAH Lugares, there is a rectangular building with a sunken patio, a patio with three pyramidal platforms, and a ball court. There is also the Rampa de los Animales, which connects to that court.

The INAH guide mentions three temples, the ramp, and the Templo de los Arquitectos, also called the Sunken Patio. In other words, this is a complex made up of several buildings grouped together.

As you walk, notice how the landscape changes. According to INAH Lugares, the city occupied six low hills, with terraces and retaining walls. That means every path climbs, descends, and winds around the hills. A retaining wall is one that holds the earth of a terrace in place so that it does not slide.

UNESCO considers that Xochicalco had three levels: a low one, an intermediate one, and a high one. According to Hirth, the city grew very quickly around the year six hundred and relocated between ten thousand and fifteen thousand people.

The next stops take place in that zone. There is no need to hurry.

texto.pregunta: Myth: Xochicalco occupies a single hill.
texto.respuesta: Reality: According to INAH Lugares, it occupied six low hills, with terraces and walls.
